title: Power Rankings: Spurs on the climb
heading: 2013-14 Power Rankings: Week 3
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Any doubt that the Spurs, before they get to the stuff that really matters, are going to win at least 50 games for the 15th consecutive season? In this purportedly mopey state after what happened in the Finals -- and with Tim Duncan producing at unrecognizable levels -- they're only on a 74-8 pace.

rankings.summaryHtml: Fun footnote about Indy's 9-0 start: It was the league's longest unbeaten run to open the season since the Mavericks went 14-0 in 2002-03 ... before finally losing at Indiana. Mark your calendars: Exactly one month to go until Dec. 18 ... when the Pacers go to Miami for the first time this season.

rankings.summaryHtml: Some decent trivia to occupy Heat-minded folks out there while waiting to see how long it takes the two-time reigning champs to get serious and lock in defensively: D-Wade is two just swats away from passing Dennis Johnson (675) as the best shot-blocker in league history at 6-4 and under.

rankings.summaryHtml: History awaits for Chris Paul if he reaches the 10-point and 10-assist plateaus in Monday's home date with Memphis. CP3 hit those benchmarks in all 10 games so far and will tie Magic Johnson's all-time record of 11 in a row to start the season (set in 1990-91) if he can do it one more time.

rankings.summaryHtml: Maybe this is a myopic way to look at last week's big anniversary in the Bay Area, but give the Dubs this as they commemorate three years of Joe Lacob's ownership: They're definitely not the Power Rankings punching bags they used to be. Golden State leads the league with six double-digit wins so far.

rankings.summaryHtml: Beating the Spurs early on, as they often do at home, failed to cause much of a stir, but I'd say that the Blazers and their fortified bench have everyone's attention now after six straight wins and four of them outside of Portland from the gang that closed out 2012-13 on a 4-19 slide in road games.

rankings.summaryHtml: How do you move past being on the wrong end of Andre Iguodala sinking the first Golden State buzzer-beater in the regular season since Monta Ellis in January 2007? Watching tape of Westbrook's sharpness in the last two games -- after he shot 34.8 percent from the field in his first five -- is a good start.

rankings.summaryHtml: Normally you'd presume that playing six games in the first 17 days of the season would be a problem in the eyes of hard-driving Bulls coach Tom Thibodeau. Yet it would appear that easing into things was a good thing for Derrick Rose judging by the six 3s he just tossed in to slay Indiana.

rankings.summaryHtml: Among the reasons why the Dwight Howard/Omer Asik tandem hasn't worked: Houston looks better offensively when it plays faster and can up the tempo with Omri Casspi or Terrence Jones at the 4. Newsy development overshadowed by all the Asik stuff: Jeremy Lin's shooting appears to have improved dramatically.

rankings.summaryHtml: The sleeve on Dirk Nowitzki has the locals almost as jittery as the up-and-down Cowboys, but leave it to my man @BallinWithBryan to do the math and compute that No. 41 is shooting .512 from the field (22-for-43), .563 on 3s (9-for-16) and averaging 21.7 PPG since slipping it over his left knee.

The Griz do appear to have responded, though, with Z-Bo in particular off to a gaudy start on Memphis' trip to Cali.

rankings.summaryHtml: Interesting theory volunteered last week by ex-Sun Marcin Gortat, who says the new defensive coordinator in Phoenix -- Mike Longabardi -- is as much of an impact newcomer in the desert as Eric Bledsoe or boss Jeff Hornacek. All four losses by just 13 points combined for the Cinderella Suns so far.

rankings.summaryHtml: Brett Brown has rightly earned many kudos for the early returns on his leap to head coaching off of Gregg Popovich's bench. Just don't ignore Mike Budenholzer's solid start in Atlanta, where Pop's longest-serving disciple has Horford and Millsap clicking and the Hawks scoring the ball freely.

rankings.summaryHtml: For all the justifiable raves about the big steps Anthony Davis has taken, there's really only one guy on the Pels' roster who can loosen up the D and make The Unibrow's life easier. You saw it Saturday night when Ryan Anderson made his floor-spacing return from a broken toe with six quick 3s against Philly.

rankings.summaryHtml: Pains me to say it, as an admitted JaVale McGee enthusiast (see last week's comment), but Denver's guards are getting to the bucket better without McGee in the middle. Kenneth Faried's positive response to trade speculation and Wilson Chandler's return, even on a minutes restriction, haven't hurt, either.

rankings.summaryHtml: You'll recall last season's Bobcats, under Mike Dunlap, actually had a better record at this juncture ... albeit by one win at 6-4. What's happening now just has a more sustainable feel, built around the stiffer D demanded by Steve Clifford and the prospect of regular frontcourt productivity from Big Al.

rankings.summaryHtml: As if to remind potential suitors that he should be high on the list of Established Vets Likely To Be Traded alongside Jameer Nelson, Arron Afflalo is already halfway to last season's eight 25-point games. The flip side: Victor Oladipo's nine TOs against Dallas reminded you how raw this team really is.

rankings.summaryHtml: The good news for Mike Brown: He's already lasted twice as long in his second Cleveland stint than he did with the Lakers last season. The legitimately worrisome news: Brown's Cavs are firmly in the top three of the Team Tension rankings. Which raises eyebrows this early into a new coach's reign.

MSG ... Madison Square Gumption.

rankings.summaryHtml: Score one for Mo Cheeks amid one of the NBA's more disappointing starts: Josh Smith responded to his maiden benching in Detroit by becoming the first player since Hakeem Olajuwon in April 1994 with 21 points, 8 boards, 7 assists, 5 steals and 4 blocks, sparking the Pistons to a much-needed road win in Sacramento.

Of course not! Thoroughly rhetorical question.

Outside of Boogie's big numbers and lil' Isaiah Thomas producing more than anyone ever expected, Sacramento's new owners are getting a harsh and immediate dose of NBA reality.
